findings.title: Error IDs are paired with nodestore results by position, so a missing or cache-reordered event gives later errors the wrong ID and content
findings.description: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` in `error_ids` order, then runs `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` does not return one entry per requested ID in that order. In `src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:174-210`, cache hits are appended after uncached rows (`items.update(cache_items)`). The Django backend's `_get_bytes_multi` (`src/sentry/nodestore/django/backend.py:48-49`) returns only rows that exist. If any referenced event is missing from nodestore, the k-th error ID is paired with the next stored event's data. The `if data is not None` filter does not catch this, because on that backend missing IDs are absent rather than `None`. Each later error then gets the wrong `id`, `title`, `message` and `timestamp`, and that text goes into the Seer prompt. Pair by node ID instead: iterate `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Error timestamps in seconds are compared with replay event timestamps in milliseconds, so every error is emitted before the first recording event
findings.description: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors and events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error side comes from the nodestore event `timestamp`, which is epoch seconds: `Event.datetime` calls `datetime.fromtimestamp(self.data["timestamp"])` (`src/sentry/eventstore/models.py:117-118`). The recording side is epoch milliseconds: `src/sentry/replays/testutils.py:32-33` (`ms()`), and `timestampMs` is documented as "in milliseconds" in `static/app/utils/replays/types.tsx`. A seconds value (~1.7e9) is always below a millisecond value (~1.7e12), so every error is yielded before the first recording event. Errors are never interleaved with the breadcrumbs, and the "at {timestamp}" text shows seconds beside millisecond breadcrumb times. The new tests use seconds on both sides, so they cannot detect this. Convert one side to the other's unit before comparing.

findings.title: The mutual-exclusion check treats `age: 0` as absent, so a report with both `age` and `timestamp` is accepted when `age` is zero
findings.description: `validate_timestamp` uses `if self.initial_data.get("age"):`, which is falsy for `0`. `age` has no `min_value`, so `{"timestamp": 1640995200000, "age": 0}` passes both validators even though the endpoint's own rule says the two fields cannot coexist. The tests only use nonzero values (`test_mixed_fields` uses `age=1`). Check for key presence (`"age" in self.initial_data`) instead of truthiness, and make the same change to the `timestamp` check in `validate_age`.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are filtered only after a search term is typed
findings.description: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`, line 34) is applied only in the filter branch. When `searchQuery.trim()` is empty, the early return at lines 61-63 returns `sorted` unfiltered, so the hidden attributes are shown by default and disappear once the user types. Apply the hidden filter before the early return.

findings.title: The table-widget placeholder ignores query results when its flag is on
findings.description: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the new branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty `data` and `meta`. `result.data` and `result.meta` never reach the table, so every dashboard table widget renders empty for an org with that flag. I found no backend registration for `use-table-widget-visualization` (only `user-feedback-ai-summaries` is in `src/sentry/features/temporary.py`), so this branch appears unreachable today. Pass `result` through before the flag is registered, or remove the branch.
